name: Svydovets Ridge
description: A green ridge of meadows and glacial lakes in the Ukrainian Carpathians, from Kvasy over Blyznytsia to Chorna Tysa. The track links the stops; those without verified coordinates are placed along it.

kvasy.name: Kvasy
kvasy.text: A village on the Black Tisza where the climb begins.

brailka.name: Brailka Meadow
brailka.text: Shepherds summer here, and cheese is made the old way.

blyznytsia.name: Blyznytsia
blyznytsia.text: The highest point of Svydovets, two green twin summits.

drahobrat.name: Drahobrat
drahobrat.text: The highest ski resort in Ukraine, quiet in summer.

stih.name: Stih
stih.text: A rounded summit on the main ridge.

vorozheska.name: Lake Vorozheska
vorozheska.text: Two glacial lakes linked by a stream, below a steep cirque.

kotel.name: Velykyi Kotel
kotel.text: The 'Great Cauldron', named for the cirque on its side.

apshynets.name: Lake Apshynets
apshynets.text: One of the highest lakes in the Carpathians; the water stays below 12 °C.

chorna-tysa.name: Chorna Tysa
chorna-tysa.text: A village in the valley at the end of the ridge.

story.treeline: The beeches give way to spruce, then to open meadow.
story.lakes: Below the ridge, lake after lake lies in the old glacial cirques.

facts.centre-europe: Svydovets borders the place near the village of Dilove claimed as the geographical centre of Europe.
facts.nine-lakes: Svydovets has nine glacial lakes; Apshynets, Vorozheska and Dohiaska are the best known.
facts.vorozheska-depth: The upper Lake Vorozheska is 4.5 m deep, the lower one 1.9 m.
